ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image is a set of schematic diagrams of different leaf margin shapes; each leaf has a central main vein and a different outer edge. Some leaf margins are relatively smooth, some are only finely toothed, and some have obvious indentations cut inward; these indentations do not cut all the way to the main vein, but extend about halfway toward the center of the leaf. Reasoning: The question asks what feature a "cleft" leaf has. According to the diagram and the meaning of the term, cleft is not a smooth edge, nor shallow serrations, but rather the leaf edge has relatively deep indentations, with the indentations extending about halfway toward the center.
